title: Your Photo Could Reveal Your Location! Check This #Shorts
description:
Sharing a photo sometimes reveals more than pixels: some cameras save GPS metadata. Apple's Photos guide explains how to review location and turn it off in sharing options. Google Photos explains that sharing metadata varies by app, album, original-file export and location settings. Even without GPS metadata, visible landmarks may reveal places. This original animated demonstration uses only a fictional landscape and fake coordinates; no user's private location or identifiable photo is shown.

Primary sources:
Apple Photos location metadata: https://support.apple.com/guide/personal-safety/manage-location-metadata-in-photos-ips0d7a5df82/web
Google Photos sharing: https://support.google.com/photos/answer/6153599

#Privacy #EXIF #PhotoTips #LocationSafety #TechExplained #Shorts

captions.text: That photo might contain more than pixels.
Some cameras save GPS coordinates in photo metadata, revealing where a picture was taken.
Apple says sharing a photo can include that location.
Google says the behavior depends on the sharing app and settings.
On iPhone, open Photos and inspect a picture's information panel for a map.
Before sharing, tap Share, then Options, and turn Location off.
On Android, review location tagging in your Camera settings.
Some platforms remove GPS metadata, but sending an original file may preserve it.
And even without GPS, landmarks in the picture can reveal a place.
Check your photo, check the sharing method, then send.
